events.credibility_reason: Known only through Friedman's attribution; primary paper unread.
Scope (n = 15) rests on Wikipedia's citation and one abstract snippet; Friedman lists 14 as only 'found'.

Self-hosted on ResearchGate/Academia only, no arXiv or journal; no engagement in ~22 months on a problem whose resolution would be news; Wikipedia's 2025-2026 revisions still call it a conjecture; the reported argument defines side length via triangular lattices only, which does not reach the hard lower bound for arbitrary packings; author and content known only from one search summary.

why: The pre-snapshot proofs of single triangular instances (n = 6, 10, 15) are scored case, since each settles a restriction of the universal claim by proof rather than by search; numerical work (Graham–Lubachevsky, Amore) is instances. Oler 1961 proves s(n) for triangular n, which the statement presupposes, not the n−1 equality, so none. Joós, Melissen–Schuur, Erdenebaatar and Singh concern different counts, containers or problems: variant. The only in-window candidate, the Nguyen document, claims the whole conjecture but carries several F10 signals together (self-hosted, no uptake for ~22 months on a landmark claim, later Wikipedia revisions still call it open, a reported lattice-only argument that misses the hard direction), so not_credible. Its date is year-precision but the one summary gives December 2024, which places it after 26 January; that call does not matter given not_credible.
doubts: The Nguyen document was never read; its author, date and content come from one search summary. Payan's exact scope and the attribution of the 14-circle case are disputed between Wikipedia and Friedman. Journal publication was taken as digestion for the old papers, none of which were read.
